controls.name: TLS-protected settlement report retrieval
controls.description: The Reconciler Job retrieves the daily settlement report from the payment processor's reporting API over HTTPS, so settlement data in transit across tb-001 is protected by TLS.
limitations: Relies on public CA and network integrity; documentation does not describe any additional integrity checks beyond generic HTTPS.

controls.name: Billing Database reachable only from Reconciler in application subnet
controls.description: The Billing Database is a managed relational database that holds billing records and discrepancy summaries and is reachable only from the Reconciler Job inside the application subnet, restricting direct network access.

controls.name: Managed database encryption at rest (asserted org control)
controls.description: The organizational controls catalog asserts a managed-db-encryption control, implying that managed databases such as the Billing Database inherit encryption at rest from the cloud platform.
limitations: Evidence asserts an organizational managed-db-encryption control but does not show specific encryption-at-rest configuration for this Billing Database instance.

controls.name: Organizational secrets vault (asserted)
controls.description: The organizational controls catalog asserts a secrets-vault control, indicating that workloads such as the Reconciler Job are expected to obtain service credentials from a managed secrets vault.
limitations: Source material does not show how the Reconciler Job's service credential is stored, retrieved, or which specific secrets service provides it.

controls.name: Reconciler authenticates to payment processor reporting API
controls.description: The Reconciler Job authenticates to the payment processor's reporting API using a service credential issued by the processor for this integration.
limitations: Documentation does not describe additional verification of the correctness of settlement report contents beyond HTTPS and API authentication.

mappings.applicability_reason: Settlement reports and discrepancy summaries are sensitive billing data [evd-004] handled by the Reconciler Job [evd-001, evd-002] and transmitted over HTTPS between the internal Reconciler and the external payment processor across tb-001 [evd-002], so the system both stores and transmits restricted data across a network boundary it does not control, matching req-DATA-001’s applicable conditions.
mappings.suppressed_conclusion: Did not conclude that encryption at rest for the managed Billing Database is absent or inadequate solely because documentation lacks detailed encryption configuration for this managed service.
mappings.suppressed_by: req-DATA-001 common_false_positives: absent encryption detail for a managed service that encrypts by default

mappings.applicability_reason: req-WEBHOOK-001 applies where the system exposes an endpoint that accepts events from an external platform. The documentation states that the Reconciler Job is a scheduled batch workload that pulls the settlement report from the payment processor and exposes no inbound interface [evd-002], so events are effectively polled rather than delivered to a webhook endpoint, matching the requirement’s non-applicable condition that inbound events are polled by the system rather than delivered to it.

documentation_gaps.title: Settlement report authenticity beyond HTTPS is undocumented
documentation_gaps.description: The documentation describes the Reconciler Job retrieving the daily settlement report from the payment processor’s reporting API over HTTPS [evd-001, evd-002] using a service credential [evd-003], and using that data to compute discrepancy summaries written to the Billing Database for finance review [evd-002, evd-004, evd-005]. However, it does not state whether there are any additional mechanisms to assure the authenticity and integrity of the settlement data beyond generic HTTPS server authentication—such as certificate pinning, signed or hashed report files, or independent cross-checks with another channel. Because threat thr-001 involves spoofed or modified settlement reports being accepted by the Reconciler, the presence or absence of such controls materially affects whether this threat is mitigated, and the current material does not establish whether any exist.
documentation_gaps.importance: Determining whether settlement reports from the payment processor are independently authenticated or cross-checked would clarify whether spoofed or intercepted reports, as in threat thr-001, remain a plausible risk or are already mitigated by design.
requested_evidence: Integration or architecture documentation describing any content-level integrity or authenticity checks on settlement reports (for example, signed report files, checksums, or certificate pinning) and where they are enforced.
Documentation of any independent reconciliation or secondary channel used to confirm the correctness of settlement totals received from the payment processor.

documentation_gaps.title: Storage and retrieval of the Reconciler service credential is not described
documentation_gaps.description: System-overview documentation states that the Reconciler authenticates to the payment processor’s reporting API with a service credential issued by the processor and provisioned through the standard workload deployment [evd-003], and the organizational controls catalog asserts a secrets-vault control [evd-006, evd-007]. The architecture does not describe where this credential is stored, how it is retrieved at runtime, or which secrets-management system provides it, so it is unclear whether the credential’s custody actually follows the organization’s managed secret-store standard.
documentation_gaps.importance: Clarifying how the Reconciler’s service credential is stored and accessed would determine whether long-lived provider credentials are held in a managed secret store as expected (for example, under req-SECRET-001) or whether additional controls are needed.
requested_evidence: Deployment or configuration documentation showing which secret store holds the Reconciler Job’s service credential, how access to that secret is controlled, and how the credential reaches the running workload.
Any organizational standard or runbook that links the asserted secrets-vault control to this specific integration.

catalog_gap_candidates.concern: The system relies on a daily settlement report retrieved from an external payment processor’s HTTPS reporting API [evd-001, evd-002, evd-003], and threat thr-001 considers spoofing or interception of that outbound HTTPS connection so that attacker-controlled settlement data is accepted. The catalog contains a requirement for verifying authenticity of inbound webhooks (req-WEBHOOK-001) and for documenting data sent to external processors (req-TPI-001), but no requirement explicitly covers additional authenticity or integrity checks for high-impact data that is polled from an external API over HTTPS (for example, certificate pinning, signed reports, or independent cross-checks).

nearest_requirements.why_not: req-WEBHOOK-001 governs authenticity verification for inbound events where the system exposes a webhook endpoint; it is explicitly non-applicable when events are polled by the system rather than delivered. The Reconciler polls the payment processor’s reporting API over outbound HTTPS and exposes no inbound webhook [evd-002], so this requirement does not cover integrity of polled responses.

req-TPI-001 addresses documentation of what customer data is sent to an external processor and the processor’s retention and usage terms; it does not ask for controls that verify the authenticity or correctness of data returned from that processor. Threat thr-001 is about forged or modified settlement data received from the payment processor rather than about data the system sends or the processor’s retention behavior.
